title: Release Quiet Window: Sentinel Protocol & Ops Notes
content:
Purpose
This doc captures an operational pattern were calling the 'quiet window sentinel' — a short, high-focus observation period immediately after enabling a canary or A/B variant. The goal is to (1) detect noisy failures early, (2) centralize human + automated checks during the highest-risk minutes, and (3) provide a repeatable comms + rollback choreography across product, SRE, and support.

Why a Quiet Window?
- LLM rollouts can produce signal that appears later (drift, hallucination spikes, regression in quality metrics) or quickly (latency tail increases, 5xx bursts).
- We observed that a focused watch window (5-30 minutes depending on exposure) reduces incident-to-rollback time and lowers blast radius.
- Combines short synthetic traffic probes, curated user slice observation, and explicit human guardrails.

When to use
- Any canary with >0.5% traffic exposure for production routes.
- New model family, quantization profile change, kernel/runtime change, or routing policy modifications.
- A/B features that alter prompt templates or reranker thresholds.

Quiet Window Modes (choose one)
- Micro (5 minutes): short-lived model variant (tiny cohort, fast feedback). Use for small config tweaks.
- Standard (15 minutes): default for single-region canaries and UI-visible changes.
- Extended (30+ minutes): use when change affects batch rerankers, long-context workloads, or introduces new external API calls.

Roster & Roles (explicit)
- Activation lead (Product PM): coordinates start/stop and stakeholder comms.
- On-call SRE: watches infra signals, can throttle/scale, and execute rollback.
- Model owner (ML Eng): watches quality evals and prompt-level failures.
- Support lead: watches customer tickets and triages urgent reports.
- Canary steward (optional): developer that knows the change and can triage quickly.

Sentinel Rules (automated + human)
- Automated Sentinels (must be configured before activation):
  - P95 latency increase > 25% relative to baseline over a 3-minute sliding window => automated alert
  - 5xx rate >= 0.5% absolute or 3x relative increase over baseline => page SRE
  - Token error rate (model decode failures / token stream interruptions) >= 0.1% => alert to ML owner
  - Regression on key quality signal (BLEU-like surrogate / rerank NDCG drop) > 4% relative => alert ML + PM
  - Synthetic probe failure rate > 2 failures in last 60 probes => notify activation lead
- Human Sentinels (during the window):
  - Quick UX walkthrough on a pre-populated checklist (owner runs 5 saved queries from diverse slices)
  - Scan sample outputs for obvious hallucinations or content regressions (5 examples per slice)
  - Check for customer-facing errors in the last 10 minutes in support dashboard

Communication Scripts (copy/paste ready)
- On start (Activation lead to #canary-ops):
  "[QuietWindow START] variant=v2.3-quant, mode=standard, exposure=2%, window=15m. SRE: monitor p95/p99, 5xx. ML: watch quality signals. Support: watch ticket stream. if any sentinel fires, state 'SENTINEL-FIRED' and escalate. Link: <link-to-runbook>"
- Sentinel fired (automated alert to channel):
  "[SENTINEL] metric=p95-latency threshold=25% baseline=220ms observed=320ms. Action: SRE please investigate and consider throttle/rollback. Activation lead: convene war room if not resolved in 3 minutes. QuietWindow-id=qw-2026-02-15-amp"
- Rollback approved (Activation lead -> #canary-ops and @oncall):
  "[ROLLBACK] variant=v2.3-quant -> rolling back to v2.2. Reason: p95 spike + 5xx spike. Time=2026-02-15T10:08Z. Initiated by Asha K. Postmortem owner assigned: Priya N."

Decision Matrix (minutes to act)
- Safety-critical sentinel (5xx spike, user-facing errors): immediate rollback window (<= 5 minutes). If unresolved after 3 minutes, rollback.
- Latency tail / infra but no functional errors: SRE to scale and watch for 10 minutes; if persists, rollback.
- Quality metric regression (NDCG / eval set): ML owner to validate sample set; if confirming regression and >4% drop, pause traffic and rollback if no mitigation within 10 minutes.

Sampling & Synthetic Probes
- Before activation, register 20 synthetic probes covering short, medium, long sequences and edge tokens. Probes should include known hard prompts and previously identified failure modes.
- Probe cadence: every 10s for Micro, every 20s for Standard, every 30s for Extended.
- Record model output hashes to quickly identify drift or non-deterministic behavior.

A/B Specific Notes
- For A/B experiments with metric-driven decisions, reserve a holdback cohort of >=1% to validate population differences.
- Power: dont rely on quiet window for statistical significance — treat the window as operational safety, not hypothesis test.
- If the A arm is below target on offline eval but not firing sentinels, schedule extended observation (24h) and run powered analysis.

Runbook Checklist (pre-activation)
- [ ] Update the rollout config with quiet_window settings (mode, cadence, probes)
- [ ] Attach linked PR and confluence spec to rollout ticket
- [ ] Confirm roster & escalation list: whos watching live
- [ ] Smoke test on staging with same quantization/kernel
- [ ] Schedule a 15-min "watch" calendar invite with required participants

During Quiet Window: quick ops checklist
- Activation lead starts window with canned message (see scripts)
- SRE watches latency, error micros, infra autoscaling behavior
- ML owner runs quick eval on 30 recent user samples + 20 probes
- Support lead monitors for spikes in UI errors & top-5 affected customers
- If a sentinel triggers, post full context to #canary-ops and start escalation protocol

Post-window responsibilities
- If no sentinels: activation lead posts "quiet window passed" and moves variant out of canary state per rollout plan
- If a sentinel fired but was mitigated: create a follow-up ticket; require a 24h extended observation and root-cause tracking
- If rollback was executed: kick off a postmortem within 48 hours and attach logs, sample outputs, and timeline

Unresolved / open questions (for team)
- Do we want a unified numeric severity score combining P95 delta, 5xx, and quality drop to guide automatic rollback decisions? (tradeoff: simpler automation vs. edge-case tuning)
- How should we handle multi-region canaries where one region shows a regression and another does not? (propose: region-isolate + hold global traffic)
- Should quiet window be mandatory for all quantization profile changes? (suggest yes; high risk)

Examples & field notes (real incidents condensed)
- Incident: v2.1-quant rolled out without probes. After 12m, p99 increased 3x due to kernel mismatch for long context. Outcome: 7m time-to-rollback; recommendation: require a long-context probe for quant/compile changes.
- Incident: A/B reranker tweak passed infra checks but caused NDCG drop on the finance slice. Sentinel on rerank NDCG fired and ML owner rolled back before customer impact. Quiet window prevented a large escalation.

Quick references
- Slack: #canary-ops, #sre-oncall, #ml-prod
- Confluence spec: confluence:CR-452-quiet-window-spec
- Rollout config repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-configs/pull/278

Appendix: Minimum embedding of sentinels in config (example CLI)
- Note: ops cli snippet below is illustrative, update prior to activation:
  ./redwood-rollout start --variant v2.3-quant --exposure 2% --quiet-window mode=standard,cadence=20s,probes=20,probes-file=canary-probes.json

Notes to self (author)
- Priya to confirm whether support dashboard can surface top-10 failing customers in a 5-minute window (action: Priya N).
- Add a template for post-rollout status message with slots for metrics (p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, sample links)

If you read one thing: the quiet window is about choreography. The tooling will improve, but explicitly assigning watchers, probes, and short escalation timeboxes is what actually reduces blast radius.
